text:
Alex Kim: Heads-up: seeing a spike of scheduling + runtime failures in eu-west GPU nodepool after the kernel patch window overnight. Pods get Scheduled but then crash during GPU init. Suspect kernel module / CUDA driver mismatch + device-plugin ordering change. Posting quick logs.
Priya Patel: oh no. did the gpu-operator DS get updated to 1.8 during the rollout? that release changed advertise ordering iirc.
Alex Kim: yes, the operator was auto-rolled to 1.8.0 at 02:10 UTC via our canary channel. node kernel updated to 5.15.0-101 at 02:05.
Samir Rao: sample node dmesg + device plugin output:

```
[   12.345678] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
[   12.346789] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and kernel version mismatch
[   12.347890] nvidia: probe failed with -22
```

```
I0603 02:15:31.123456 1 device_plugin.go:142] advertising 2 GPUs
E0603 02:15:31.223456 1 device_plugin.go:210] Runtime setup failed: failed to open /dev/nvidia0: no such file or directory
```

Jia Chen: logs show device-plugin advertising before driver/nvidia node plugin finished registering devices. if advertise happens too early kubelet will schedule pods onto GPU-less node.
Alex Kim: exactly. cluster is ending up with Scheduled -> CrashLoopBackOff for GPU workloads. Costly since we're retrying many inference workers.
infra-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: GPU nodepool eu-west-1b has 18/40 nodes reporting driver init errors. Incident created: INC-2026-331
Priya Patel: immediate mitigation: cordon the problematic nodes and redirect scheduled capacity to the spare pool (eu-west-1a). we have autoscaler headroom in 1a.
Samir Rao: steps I'd take now:
1) cordon + drain affected nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-eu-*-3 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-eu-*-3`
2) rollback gpu-operator to 1.7.2: `kubectl -n gpu-operator rollout undo daemonset/gpu-operator` (confirm revision)
3) force driver reinstall via DS that runs nvidia-installer (or DKMS) on rebooted nodes

Jia Chen: also check kubelet version + driver kernel module ABI: `modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic` and `uname -r`. if vermagic != uname -r, DKMS won't help until kernel headers match.
Alex Kim: I'm going to cordon/evict the worst nodes now. tagging @Priya to coordinate traffic shift.
Priya Patel: on it. shifting inference traffic off eu-west-1b to 1a. updating traffic-routes and autoscaler targets. will post when done.
Samir Rao: if rollback is blocked (e.g., image no longer available), we can patch the device-plugin to delay advertise until `/dev/nvidia*` visible. quick patch snippet:

```
if len(listDevices()) == 0 {
  sleep 5s
  retry
}
advertise()
```

That buys time until drivers are present.
Alex Kim: good fallback. also let's not waste quota: throttle retries by reducing parallelism on the Job controller for inference workers.
Jia Chen: noted. I've also opened a short playbook entry for this: kernel-driver mismatch -> cordon -> rollback operator -> reinstall drivers -> uncordon. include kubelet modinfo checks.
infra-bot: Update: rollback job started by ops runbook (user: Alex Kim). Watch: ds/gpu-operator@1.7.2
Priya Patel: traffic shifted, autoscaler bumped 1a by +6 nodes, no errors in 1a. eu-west-1b still failing driver init on 14 nodes.
Samir Rao: rolling rollback now. if hotpatching, prefer DKMS packaged build we tested last month. otherwise reimage to kernel that matches module build.
Alex Kim: rollback to 1.7.2 completed at 03:08 UTC. restarting daemonset on nodes as they come up.
Jia Chen: I'm seeing device nodes reappear on 4/40 so far. `kubectl get nodes -owide` shows kernel 5.15.0-101 still, modinfo vermagic matching on fixed nodes.
Priya Patel: nice. keeping cordon until we verify stable pod runtimes for 30m. lowering job parallelism to 10% for now.
Samir Rao: action items postmortem:
- Pin gpu-operator image for non-canary nodepools for the next 72h
- Add readiness check to device-plugin so it doesn't advertise GPUs before /dev present
- Add hook in rollout pipeline to validate kernel/driver vermagic match on a canary node
- Cost note: ~3 hours of increased autoscaling in eu-west, estimate extra $1.2k in compute

Alex Kim: good list. I'll create the PR for the device-plugin readiness guard and the pinning change. assigning follow-ups in the incident ticket.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-331 updated: status -> mitigated. responders: Alex Kim, Priya Patel, Samir Rao, Jia Chen.

Alex Kim: thanks team. will leave nodes cordoned for another 30m and then gradually uncordon as we validate. :thumbsup:
